journal:
When I was young, I was always told to avoid the forest bank along the river, I remember my mother scolding me once after spotting me and a few friends playing on the forests edge "Stay away from that tree line! A monsterous creature lives in there feeding on foolish children who stray too close". I'd be lying if I said that didn't terrify me and my friends. We'd always been told stories about the troll, memories passed down from the alderman who himself had been told it by the one before. Just to mere mention of the creature was enough to send half the village into a spiralling panic.

"He turned our milk sour" they'd cry, "He ate one of my lambs" another would bleat out; it seemed to me at one point that everything bad that had ever happened in the village, this creature appeared to be the root cause. I wouldn't say I was a disobedient child, maybe terminally curious would be a better description, but hearing all of these stories just made me want to steel my resolve and find out how true it all was.

Me and a few friends hatched a plan, we'd wait until just before dawn and sneak out to the forests edge, we daren't go when it was dark. I remember by the time I'd got to the forests edge the others had lost their nerve and bolted back to the village presumably to tell the parents what foolish endeavour I was undertaking, but I had to know.

I did find the creature in the end, and it seemed like a gentle soul. I never told anyone about it, and I would sometimes visit on my birthdays or when I was feeling particularly sad, it seemed to understand how I felt, even though we couldn't not make sense of each other. I visited for one last time this summer past, for I am far too frail to be able to make the journey again. It seemed to understand this would was our last meeting, its timeless and pleasant smile reassuring me everything would be all right.
prompt: Low beside the riverbank in the rain, a single lantern between them lights the troll's craggy face as it holds a huge leaf over the boy's head and the boy laughs up at it.

music.why: A gentle troll sheltering a laughing boy under a leaf by lantern light in the rain, and a lifelong secret friendship ending in a quiet farewell, call for something soft, close and storybook.
